correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the finite covering and replacement logic for the actual 166-word code. Separate Python/NumPy enumeration, reading all 166 public codewords directly, evaluated the entire 6^8=1,679,616 ambient space, all codeword distances, coverage multiplicities and all private regions. Obtained exactly 7,173 multiplicity-one points with sizes 8..105, all private points at distance exactly 5 from the other 165 words, and 165 singleton repair intersections plus the sole {51004501,51004441} doubleton. Mathematically deletion affects only private points; y repairs iff d(y,x)<=4 for all private x. Therefore all single deletions have radius exactly 5 and exactly one nontrivial replacement retains radius four. The published upper bound alone was not used as proof of the new properties.
residual_risks: Theorem concerns fixed published code, not global optimality of size 166 or multicodeword moves.

value.rationale: This is a mathematically motivated exact local-exchange classification of a distinguished contemporary 166-word Hamming covering-code witness. The primary source uses private coverage and delete-and-repair in its descent search; the exact fact that 165 deletions have no alternative one-word repair, and one has only one, identifies the rigorous boundary of single-word exchange exploration at that record. The 7173 private words and all deletion-radius-five classification describe natural code irredundancy and sensitivity. This is beyond rechecking the published K6(8,4)<=166 cover and could guide future searches requiring larger coordinated repair moves; no claim of global optimality or large structural theorem.
residual_risks: The specialized invariant is of one explicit representative; not general q-ary bounds or global code classification.
